title: Highest weight theory, Part II: nilpotent orbits and weight patterns
summary: Extend the existing highest-weight roadmap by zero-inclusive sl2 triples, their nilpotent adjoint orbits and increasing representation filtrations. Prove recognition using classical standard and half-spin modules and independently certified exceptional adjoint profiles. Construct geometric weight patterns and prove that they determine the positive real part of a complex semisimple parameter. The integral completion and category-O briefs have independent successor owners, recorded under restructure.
readme: Build on the existing LieHighestWeight roadmap. This continuation owns nilpotent adjoint orbits, zero-inclusive triples, representation filtrations and their recognition, exceptional finite root certificates and geometric weight patterns. The full target statements, APIs, tests, sources and conventions are in research/blueprint/readmes/LieHighestWeightPartII.md. The independent p-adic enveloping-algebra and completed-category-O continuations have successor briefs in the packet restructure and handoff, and are not part of these six layers.

stages.title: Nilpotent orbits and adapted triples
stages.description: Build a zero-inclusive adapter to the native sl2 triple and the nilpotent adjoint orbit interface. Prove the semisimple Jordan-centralizer reduction, Jacobson–Morozov, algebraic integration of a triple, Kostant transitivity over a fixed nilpotent and conjugacy from the neutral element. Work over any algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, and use current library trace identities rather than replanning them.

stages.title: Representation filtrations and graded multiplicities
stages.description: Restrict finite Lie modules through the native sl2 basis constructor. Construct the increasing eigenfiltration W_i, identify its graded quotient with the weight-i eigenspace, and recover sl2 multiplicities by d_n−d_(n+2). Prove strictness, levelwise exactness and tensor/dual compatibility in the existing filtered-object vocabulary. Zero is a single jump at zero.

stages.title: Classical recognition and half-spin tests
stages.description: Recover classical nilpotent partitions from the standard module, prove the invariant-form parity constraints and the O-to-SO splitting criterion, and distinguish the very-even pair by a fixed Lie half-spin module. State the finite test family in each classical type with the actual Lie weight lattice; do not require descent of half-spin to SO.

stages.title: Exceptional root certificates and appendix profiles
stages.description: Use dominant labels 0,1,2, opposition and nonnegative sl2 multiplicities as necessary conditions. Construct exact adjoint root profiles, certify injectivity on the finite candidate sets independently for G2,F4,E6,E7,E8, and deduce exceptional adjoint separation. Decode all 91 CH table rows by checked profiles and cumulative sums, with root-vector witnesses for the supplied representatives; printed orbit names remain row keys. The separation proof needs no full orbit enumeration.

stages.title: Semisimple filtration recognition
stages.description: Assemble the classical and exceptional tests through fixed simple factors. Prove that simultaneous adjoint conjugacy, equality of all representation filtration dimensions and isomorphic sl2 restrictions are equivalent, including the zero algebra and zero triple. Record a finite representation test family and preserve factor labels.

stages.title: Highest weights and geometric weight patterns
stages.description: Prove the root-coset and highest-weight half-integrality tests. Define finite geometric modulus patterns for q>1 and the positive part of a complex torus element using its character lattice. Supply algebraic characters with each allowed dominant leading weight by a regular semi-invariant argument, then prove that algebraic characters separate Weyl orbits and equal representation-indexed patterns force conjugacy of positive real parts. Phases and the choice of isogeny lattice are explicit.
